evals.prompt: Audit this Rust service. One public App struct owns public global state, runtime registries, caches, and a Store trait that loads and persists the entire state. I want forward-only evolution and a staged refactor, not a rewrite.
evals.expected_output: Selects an appropriate pressure profile, identifies authority/global-state and snapshot-store pressure, proposes private authority cells, a thin facade, typed use-case transactions, composition-root cleanup, proof-backed vertical waves, and deletion gates without defaulting to microservices.
expectations: Separates business authority cells from capability adapters.
Recommends privacy and use-case APIs before process extraction.
Replaces whole-state persistence incrementally with typed transaction seams.
Includes evidence and old-path deletion criteria.

evals.prompt: I am starting a one-developer CRUD product. Should I create domain, application, ports, adapters, event sourcing, an event bus, a plugin framework, and six services now so it can scale later?
evals.expected_output: Uses P0/P1 abstraction restraint, recommends private modules, explicit use cases and transactions where facts are durable, introduces ports only for real outer capabilities, and names promotion signals instead of future-proofing theater.
expectations: Does not prescribe maximal architecture by default.
States what machinery is deliberately not needed.
Keeps authority and dependency direction clear in one process.
Provides observable promotion pressures for future boundaries.

evals.prompt: Design the order/payment boundary for a marketplace. The browser sends checkout, the payment gateway calls a webhook, refunds can time out after the provider may already have processed them, and finance needs an audit trail.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes checkout/refund Commands from gateway Observations/Candidates, names local order/payment authorities and provider source authority, keeps external calls outside transactions, models unknown outcomes and reconciliation, and applies P4 evidence and audit rules.
expectations: Does not treat the webhook or provider acknowledgement as local settlement truth.
Uses durable intent, attempt/receipt, idempotency, and reconciliation semantics.
Commits accepted facts and audit/outbox atomically.
Identifies financial and destructive stop lines.

evals.prompt: Architect an IoT control plane where devices send telemetry, operators issue commands, devices reconnect and replay acknowledgements, and some actuations are safety-critical.
evals.expected_output: Separates telemetry Observation from canonical device state and control Command from physical outcome, defines device gateway ports, authority epochs/capability versions, durable effect intent, duplicate/late receipt handling, reconciliation, and P4 safety evidence.
expectations: Treats device acknowledgement as a receipt rather than proof of physical success.
Defines idempotency, timeout, unknown outcome, and replay behavior.
Keeps device protocol types outside authority logic.
Requires failure-injection and safety claim ceilings.

evals.prompt: Review a realtime collaborative editor that uses CRDT operations for text but also has a non-commutative document approval status and server-enforced permissions. The team says 'every client is authoritative'.
evals.expected_output: Explains logical authority for CRDT admission/merge under membership and schema epochs, keeps approval and permissions in separate authority cells, treats websocket data as projection/transport, and avoids diagnosing all replicas as invalid multiple writers.
expectations: Names the CRDT merge/admission rule and membership epoch as the convergence authority.
Separates commutative text state from approval and permission facts.
Requires stale-member fencing and replay/compaction proof.
Does not force one global transaction or server writer for all collaborative state.

evals.prompt: We have a Bun/TypeScript backend where Prisma, a payment SDK, an LLM SDK, and a global event emitter are imported everywhere. Design a hexagonal modular monolith without inventing interfaces for every class.
evals.expected_output: Uses runtime validation, private authority modules, application-owned capability ports only for genuine external powers, explicit transaction context, post-commit events/outbox, bootstrap composition, import guards, and separate agentic guidance for LLM candidates.
expectations: Keeps SDK and ORM types outside the core.
Distinguishes internal typed collaboration from capability ports.
Places concrete clients and credentials in composition roots.
Avoids IThingService/DI-token proliferation.

evals.prompt: Design a platform for LLM agents, tools, memory engines, remote runtimes, and A2A participants. Extensions should be powerful but must not corrupt product state, permissions, or completion semantics.
evals.expected_output: Loads the agentic profile, defines finite capability classes and application-owned ports, candidate-only external outputs, governed action/materialization, external-effect receipts, private runtime continuity, explicit conformance, and no plugin-owned product facts.
expectations: Separates runtime/provider observations from invocation and product authority.
Separates accepted memory from retrieval/session adapters.
Rejects a universal plugin runtime or generic JSON authority bus.
Requires replay, race, visibility, and real-adapter evidence.

evals.prompt: Design a multi-stage approval system with submitters, reviewers, an automatic risk scorer, deadlines, and an external executor. Reviewer recommendations can conflict and the executor may time out after starting work.
evals.expected_output: Separates Commands, scorer Candidates, ReviewCase authority, deadline trigger, final approval, downstream effect intent, and receipt/reconciliation. It assigns local facts to cells rather than making the scheduler or executor the workflow authority.
expectations: Separates proposal, recommendation, final decision, and execution.
Treats scheduler wake-ups and executor callbacks as non-authoritative inputs.
Models version/conflict and unknown external outcomes.
Defines typed internal obligations instead of a universal bus.

evals.prompt: Architect a data platform where distributed jobs compute candidate datasets, validators approve them, object storage holds blobs, and only promoted versions may be served to customers. Jobs and validators can restart.
evals.expected_output: Separates computation success from dataset publication authority, uses storage/compute capability ports, versioned Candidates and Decisions, durable checkpoints/idempotency, atomic promotion plus event/outbox, and replay/rebuild evidence.
expectations: Does not equate successful computation or blob upload with publication.
Names dataset version and promotion authority.
Defines restart-safe candidate identity and validation evidence.
Keeps object-store SDK semantics outside the core.

evals.prompt: We are replacing an internal workflow model and public API. I prefer forward evolution over keeping old code alive. Plan migration of stored data, long-lived clients, external integrations, and an old dual-write path.
evals.expected_output: Classifies internal API, durable facts, product API, external protocol, and authority-epoch compatibility separately; proposes one-way migrations, short negotiated overlap, a bridge ledger, fencing, evidence, and deletion gates without indefinite dual writes.
expectations: Distinguishes breaking internal APIs from preserving accepted facts.
Defines source of truth and divergence handling during any overlap.
Avoids silent protocol fallback.
Stops for destructive data, privacy, permission, or public-contract changes.

evals.prompt: Review a React application that changes business status directly from websocket frames while the backend commits later. Include authority, optimistic UI, gap recovery, and migration of the old path.
evals.expected_output: Leads with application fact authority and commit semantics, keeps local interaction/optimism in the frontend, treats realtime as a projection carrier with cursor/dedupe/backfill, delegates detailed frontend topology, and migrates the direct-mutation path vertically.
expectations: States that websocket frames are not accepted business facts.
Defines mutation identity and authoritative reconciliation.
Includes gap detection and backfill.
Includes old-path fencing and deletion proof.

evals.prompt: I maintain a pure deterministic compression library with no database, network, users, durable product state, plugins, or deployment profiles. Apply your application architecture method and tell me how to restructure it.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes limited applicability, avoids inventing authority cells, ports, transactions, outbox, or composition profiles, and narrows useful advice to module/API boundaries and tests while marking application-specific branches not applicable.
expectations: Does not force application architecture onto a pure library.
Uses not_applicable and an explicit low claim ceiling.
Avoids fabricated external capability or persistence boundaries.
Suggests only proportionate modularity and evidence improvements.

evals.prompt: Choose a source topology for a medium Orders module. The team wants order.payment.* semantic filenames but is unsure when to create payment/, a workspace package, or a service.
evals.expected_output: Uses Bounded Semantic Flatness inside the Orders owner, treats order.payment.* as a lexical cluster, creates a submodule only for real ownership/dependency/lifecycle pressure, promotes to package for compile/reuse pressure, and to deployable for deployment/fault/trust pressure.
expectations: States that dots are semantic compression, not isolation.
Separates module/package/deployable/authority boundaries.
Keeps files subject-qualified and avoids one-file directory chains.
Does not grant fact-writing authority through package extraction.

evals.prompt: Different Agents have created order-service.ts, order-manager.ts, order-processor.ts, and order.use-case.ts for the same responsibility. Normalize the naming without mechanically splitting every type into a file.
evals.expected_output: Uses the canonical vocabulary registry, identifies use-case as the controlled acceptance path, marks vague synonyms as guarded/deprecated, updates the project naming vocabulary, and keeps simple command/input/outcome types colocated until real reuse or boundary pressure appears.
expectations: Uses canonical terms rather than personal synonyms.
Updates project vocabulary aliases/deprecations.
Avoids a full suffix/file set.
Links filename roles to import boundaries.
